title: Jaiswal and Rahul reply with 130-run stand as India reach 159 for one in Wellington
dek: India trail New Zealand by 209 after the second day of the first Test, having bowled the hosts out for 368. Henry Nicholls carried his bat for an unbeaten 175.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Yashasvi Jaiswal made 85 and KL Rahul an unbeaten 52 in an opening stand of 130 as India reached 159 for one at stumps on the second day of the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Friday, 209 runs behind the hosts' first-innings 368.

Earlier, Henry Nicholls carried his bat for an unbeaten 175 and Glenn Phillips completed his second Test century as New Zealand added 125 on the second morning. Jasprit Bumrah finished with four for 92 and Akash Deep with three for 53.

## India's reply

Jaiswal and Rahul began cautiously, playing out the first four overs without scoring, before Jaiswal took charge. He reached his half-century off 66 balls and had hit 16 fours in his 89-ball 85 when Matt Henry had him caught behind by Tom Blundell in the 28th over, New Zealand overturning the on-field decision on review, according to reports. India were 130 for one at the time.

Both openers survived chances. New Zealand missed a leg-before review against Rahul, and Phillips dropped Jaiswal, according to reports. Rahul, who reached his first Test half-century against New Zealand, was 52 not out off 116 balls at the close, with Devdutt Padikkal unbeaten alongside him; reports differ on whether Padikkal had 15 or 16. India batted 39 overs in the day.

## How the morning went

New Zealand resumed on 243 for five. India had the second new ball available from the start of play but could not break the partnership early. Nicholls and Phillips, who came together at 70 for five on Thursday afternoon, took their sixth-wicket stand to 216 before Akash Deep bowled Phillips for 118 shortly before lunch. New Zealand went to the interval on 317 for six.

The tail then went quickly. Prasidh Krishna had Nathan Smith leg before for 14, Akash Deep had Kyle Jamieson caught by Rahul for 11, and Bumrah trapped Matt Henry leg before for 1. Nicholls added 20 for the last wicket with Jacob Duffy before Anshul Kamboj had Duffy caught behind by Rishabh Pant for 4. New Zealand's innings lasted 121 overs; apart from Nicholls and Phillips, no batter passed 15.

## The bowling

- Jasprit Bumrah: 29-8-92-4
- Akash Deep: 23-7-53-3
- Anshul Kamboj: 23-5-69-2
- Prasidh Krishna: 26-2-100-1
- Washington Sundar: 20-2-45-0

India picked four fast bowlers and Washington Sundar as the only specialist spinner, leaving out Mohammed Siraj and Ravindra Jadeja.

## What is at stake

The two-Test series counts towards the 2025-27 World Test Championship, in which New Zealand lead the table and India are fourth. Shubman Gill, India's captain, has said his side need to win five or six of their remaining seven Tests to reach the final. With nine wickets in hand and three days left, India have the chance to build a first-innings lead on Saturday, early in the morning Indian time. The second Test is in Christchurch.
